question: The lecture opened the pipeline with a fact it called counterintuitive. After all of the context goes into the model, how much comes out?

options.feedback: A sentence is what you see on screen, so it is natural to assume that is the unit of output. It is not: a sentence is assembled from many separate runs of the model.
The response you read was never produced in one piece. The entire context is processed for every single token of it.

options.text: One token for every token in the context
options.feedback: The input and output are not matched one to one. However long the context is, the model's job on each run is to produce just the next token.
All of that input, your prompt, attachments, and conversation, is processed to produce a single next token. That is the whole job of one pass through the model.
